blocks.title: Sort into: Breaks the fast / Does not break the fast
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Breaks the fast, Does not break the fast.
blocks.answer: Breaks the fast: A. Eating on purpose; C. Making yourself vomit on purpose; F. Drinking water on purpose. Does not break the fast: B. Drinking by mistake, having forgotten; D. Swallowing your own saliva; E. Showering or swimming without swallowing water; G. Using a miswak; H. Tasting nothing but smelling food

questions.q: Sara eats a biscuit at 3 pm, then remembers she is fasting. What is the ruling?
questions.a: Her fast is valid: she forgot. She stops eating when she remembers and continues fasting.
questions.model: I do: 1) Was it deliberate? No. 2) Evidence: whoever forgets and eats should complete the fast (Bukhari and Muslim). 3) Ruling: the fast is valid; stop and carry on.

questions.a: Someone who can never fast, e.g. the very elderly

questions.q: Fiqh scenarios (pupil PDF), then explain each in the portal response box: a) Ali swims and swallows no water. b) Maryam has flu for three days. c) Grandad, 90, cannot fast at all. d) Yusuf drinks juice at noon on purpose.
questions.a: a) Valid. b) Excused: qada' three days later. c) Fidyah: feed a poor person for each day. d) Broken: sinful; repent and make it up, as scholars explain.
questions.model: Teacher does a): 'Swimming does not break the fast as long as no water is swallowed, so Ali's fast is valid.'

questions.q: why does Islam give exemptions from fasting?
questions.a: Islam is ease (2:185); fasting must not cause harm.

questions.q: what is the difference between qada' and fidyah?
questions.a: Qada' is making up the day; fidyah is feeding the poor when making up is impossible.

questions.q: When does the fast end each day?
Back to our ponder: what do you need to know so your fast is correct?
questions.a: Who fasts, intention, what breaks it, exemptions, qada' and fidyah.
